title: The summit
hookLine: the top of the hill is not the end: every tradition sends you back down to ordinary life, carrying what you found
carry: down the hill, with open hands
tomorrow: the hill's behind you. what's the first plain thing you'll do?

lines: HIS FACE SHINES LIKE THE SUN.
LET US MAKE HERE THREE TABERNACLES.
cards: The concert ends, the lights come up, and everybody files out to the parking lot. Matthew's Gospel has a mountaintop like that. Jesus takes Peter, James and John up a high mountain, and his face shines like the sun.
Moses and Elijah appear, talking with him. Peter blurts out: "Lord, it is good for us to be here: if thou wilt, let us make here three tabernacles." Stay.

teach.b: A bright cloud covers them, and a voice says: "This is my beloved Son, in whom I am well pleased; hear ye him." They fall on their faces. Jesus touches them and tells them to get up and not be afraid.
And then they come down the mountain.

teach.h: DOWN TO A FATHER WHO KNEELS.
teach.b: At the bottom a crowd is waiting, and a father kneels and begs mercy for his son. Matthew tells it in that order: the glory shown on the mountain, then carried down into the valley, where someone needs help.
Christians keep this story as the Transfiguration. Here's what this path shares with it.
Kuoan's ten ox pictures end the same way: not at the empty circle up high, but in the market, the herder dusty and smiling, helping with open hands. And an honest difference.
Peter, James and John come down following Jesus, the one the voice calls my beloved Son.

teach.h: DOWN THE HILL, WITH OPEN HANDS.
teach.b: Kuoan's herder comes down with no teacher ahead of him and no voice from a cloud, only a gourd and open hands. Both say the top of the hill is not the end. Five years, one hill.
What you found up here goes back down with you, into an ordinary Monday.

how: Christians keep the feast of the Transfiguration, and Matthew 17 carries the glory down to people in need; Zen students end the ox-herding pictures in the market. People on this path take their practice back into ordinary days.

o: the top of the hill, and the start of the way down
a final exam that tests everything you've learned
the highest rank a student can earn in a school

games.q: the summit and the way down: tap the pairs.
p: let us make here three tabernacles
kneels at the bottom, begging mercy

s: in Matthew, Peter offers to build three tabernacles on the mountain
it is good for us to be here, he says: stay, build, keep this.
the disciples stay on the mountain to keep the vision
they come down, and a father with a suffering son is waiting.
Kuoan's pictures and the Transfiguration teach exactly the same thing
both come down the hill; the disciples follow Jesus, the herder names no God.

games.q: your friend is back from a life-changing pilgrimage and wants to quit everything and stay at the shrine. what do both of today's stories suggest?
o: the glory is for the valley: carry it back down into ordinary life.
stay: if a place is holy, leaving it wastes the whole gift.
forget it fast; the mountaintop was only an emotional high.
games.why: Peter wanted to build tents on the mountain, but they came down to a father in need; Kuoan's herder ends in the market. both stories walk back down.

practice: If you can, walk for a minute: down a hall, down some stairs, out the door. With each step, bring one line of your own rule along, the way the herder carried his gourd into town.
If walking isn't possible now, rest your hands open on your knees for the two minutes.

wordCard.voice: The summit: the top of the hill, reached at last, and the first step of the walk back down to ordinary life.

orig.note: Greek, Matthew 17:4: it is good for us to be here.

carryVoice: Here's the last line: down the hill, with open hands. Five years of climbing, and the summit counts.
